name: Vega 1
best_known_for: Soviet Venus + Halley's Comet double mission — dropped a Venera-style lander + first interplanetary balloon aerostat into Venus's atmosphere, then continued on a 9-month cruise to fly past Halley
credit: First spacecraft of the international Halley armada. Launched 1984-12-15 on a Proton-K / D-1 from Baikonur. The 4920 kg flyby bus carried a ~1500 kg descent module that separated for Venus arrival 1985-06-11 — the lander touched down at 7.5°N, 177.8°E for 56 minutes of surface science, while a first-of-kind helium-filled balloon aerostat floated in the cloud deck at 54 km altitude for 46 hours tracking wind speeds + atmospheric structure across two thirds of the planet. The Vega-1 flyby bus then continued on its 9-month cruise to comet 1P/Halley, encountering the nucleus 1986-03-06 at 8889 km — the first Halley encounter of the armada, providing the targeting data ESA's Giotto used 8 days later for its much closer 596 km approach. Twin spacecraft Vega-2 launched 6 days later.
